Subject: Sizing + Hosting options for SAFE Health pilot

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and infra asked me to get a concise comparison of Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) vs a Private deployment for our initial pilot (HIPAA-bound). High level asks from our side:

- Expected GPU count and shape for a pilot supporting ~120 concurrent users with median session length 90s (we included sample traces).
- Latency p50/p95 targets you expect under each model and realistic SLAs.
- Security posture differences (auditing, KMS integration, network isolation).
- Cost estimate for a 3-month pilot + what changes once we scale to production.

Can you (or someone on your team) share a short recommendation and ballpark numbers by next week? Procurement would like to understand what they need to budget for. I attached the sample traces.

Appreciate it —

Sarah —

Thanks for the file and the clear asks. Looping in Marissa and Laura for commercial & SLA aspects; Jonas will help with the low-level GPU sizing and cost math.

Quick summary up front: for a 3-month pilot we typically recommend Dedicated (reserved) unless the customer requires customer-managed network/VPC or on-prem HSM. Dedicated gets you predictable throughput, simpler onboarding, and a faster path to scale; Private buys the maximum isolation and control but has a heavier lift and higher fixed cost.

I’ll attach a short two-sheet proposal with two options (Dedicated pilot vs Private pilot) — rough GPU counts, latency estimates, and a runway cost for 3 months. Important gating items we need from SAFE: SOC 2 report or equivalent, a brief network diagram for Private, and KMS/HSM requirements.

High-level numbers (ballpark):
- Dedicated pilot: 4x A10G-equivalent GPUs (continuous burst capable) with autoscaling buffer to 8 GPUs for peak. Expected p50 ~ 45-60ms per token, p95 ~ 220-300ms for your median session shapes. Estimated total infra spend (Redwood hosted) ~$85k for 3 months including support and reserved capacity uplift.
- Private pilot (VPC-hosted or on-prem appliance): baseline 6x A10G-equivalent GPUs (no shared tenancy), engineered image and networking + KMS setup. Expect slightly better p95 (~200-250ms) if deployed in your VPC with optimized networking. Estimated one-time onboarding & infra setup fee ~$45k + monthly infra equivalent to ~$95k for 3 months (higher due to engineering/setup amortization).

I’ve attached the draft proposal. If you want, we can model a midline: Dedicated with dedicated tenant (isolated pool) that gives most controls with lower setup time.

Next steps: Marissa can follow up on terms (credits/commit), and Laura can outline SLA options if you need a 99.9/99.95 tier during pilot.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sizing & hosting recommendation for SAFE Health pilot (internal)

Internal notes / pricing assumptions — please weigh in quickly: 

1) Customer profile: HIPAA-regulated SaaS; pilot expected to convert if p95 <= 300ms and unit cost < $0.007/token equivalent for triage workflows.

2) Dedicated pilot (recommended default):
- Fleet: 4x A10G-equivalent (baseline), autoscale headroom to 8x for peaks.
- Config: reserved capacity term for 3 months with short-term burst; apply a pilot credit of 25% to subsidize onboarding.
- Commercial: base infra + managed service: ~$85k total (matches Rishi). 30-day SLA standard, option to buy 99.95 for +$8k/mo.

3) Private pilot (for strict isolation):
- Fleet: 6x A10G-equivalent dedicated to SAFE; includes private control plane in their VPC.
- Work: infra engineering (network, KMS, audit logs, VPN), SOC2 gap remediation work if needed. 
- Commercials: one-time setup $45k, monthly infra amortized into pilot: total ~ $95k for 3 months.

4) Hybrid alternative (fastest path): Dedicated isolated tenant + customer-managed Egress VPC peering for audit logs. Lower setup cost (~$18k) and most security controls.

Jonas — can you confirm the GPU shapes (A10G vs A100) tradeoffs here? I assumed A10G-equivalent since that provides best cost/latency for token-heavy triage loads.

Laura — please prepare a short upsell play for how we transition from pilot to reserved capacity commit (90–180 day runway).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Exec — Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>

Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing & hosting recommendation for SAFE Health pilot (technical note)

Marissa / team — quick technical notes and a small correction to the attachment: 

- A10G-equivalent is the right starting point given SAFE's workload (short context windows, high concurrency). A100s would lower p50 marginally but drive cost 2x+; not justified for pilot.
- For Private deployments, we should budget for 2 extra GPUs during setup to warm KV caches and do perf tuning (so baseline 8 during the first 2 weeks, then 6 steady-state).
- Network: If SAFE wants end-to-end private connectivity, we need a cross-connect/VPN + flow logs; expect ~5 business days for provisioning on their side.
- Quantization/optimizations: recommend INT8 quantization profile for their model family which reduces memory and allows packing more replicas per GPU; saves ~20% monthly infra cost.

Updated quick table (ballpark):
- Dedicated: 4 baseline / 8 peak. Estimated tokens/sec average 42k, p95 220–300ms.
- Private: 6 baseline (8 warmup). Estimated tokens/sec average 50k, p95 200–260ms.

I updated fleet_proposal_v1.xlsx with a technical tab (see Drive link). If we go Private, factor in an extra 0.5 FTE for 2 months of infra ops support.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
